mappings.sourceQuestionText: I am a 4-digit number. All my digits are different. My first digit is 3 times my last digit. My second digit is one less than my first. My third digit is double my last digit. What number am I?
mappings.sourceExplanation: Last=2, First=6, no wait... Let me recalculate: 3×1=3, 3-1=2, 2×1=2, last=1 → but not 4 digits. Try: 6521 (6=3×2, 5=6-1, 2=2×1, 1). Actually: 3624
mappings.finalQuestionText: I am a 4-digit number. All my digits are different. My first digit is 3 times my last digit. My second digit is one less than my first. My third digit is double my last digit. What numbers can I be?
mappings.finalExplanation: Let the last digit be d, so the digits are 3d, 3d−1, 2d, d. The only possible last digits are 1, 2, and 3. When d=1, the digit 2 repeats, so it is invalid. When d=2, the number is 6542; when d=3, the number is 9863. Both satisfy every stated constraint.
